clue.text: Where many passengers are at length accommodated

definitions.text: Where many passengers are at length accommodated

parts.words: Where many passengers are at length accommodated
parts.note: a riddle about overnight rail travel: the passengers lie stretched out full length in berths on the train

explanation.surface: A remark about where travellers are put up, apparently after a long wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At length' seems to mean 'eventually', but it means lying full length, as people do in a train's bunks.
explanation.definitionFit: Night trains carry beds for travellers, and such a carriage or train is known by the people who doze in it.

clue.text: Cut up, going round the bend? A wash-out!

indicators.note: the cutting word travels around the bend, so its letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: to cut up bread is to slice it
a U-bend is the curved pipe under a sink, so a bend can be shaped like the letter U

explanation.surface: Someone chopped up and gone mad, the whole thing a fiasco.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going round the bend' looks like 'going mad', but it tells you SLICE goes round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A channel with a gate that lets water rush through is used to flush or scour things out.

clue.text: But expect changes

indicators.note: the word expect undergoes changes, so its letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A caution that one's expectations may shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' in its sense 'other than' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce an exclusion, as in 'everyone but me' and 'everyone save me'.

clue.text: Point in topical new presentation of old philosopher's theory

indicators.note: a new presentation of the words gives their letters in a fresh order

parts.note: N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A topical point given a new angle in a talk about an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins: N is shuffled with TOPICAL as one pool.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes ideas belonging to the Athenian teacher of Aristotle, such as his doctrine of Forms.

clue.text: Refuse to go on a register

indicators.note: the following letter is told to go on the end of the first piece

parts.note: rot is rubbish, nonsense: refuse

explanation.surface: Someone declining to be signed up on a list.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A duty roster is a list naming who serves when, a kind of register.

clue.text: Pair left in motor car

indicators.note: the one letter is placed in the body of the car word

parts.note: a coupe is a two-door motor car

explanation.surface: Two people abandoned inside a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Two of anything make a brace or duo.

clue.text: Election work can include circular letter

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: the can word takes the round letter in among its own letters

parts.note: a tin is a can
O is the round letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Campaign work involves sending out leaflets to voters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Election' and 'circular letter' suggest a campaign mailshot; election here means choosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Election in the sense of picking freely is a choice.

clue.text: Bale out after plane tip touches mountain? That's obvious!

indicators.note: the plane's tip touches the mountain, so the two sit side by side
the rearranged bale comes after the mountain piece
the tip of the plane is its first letter

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

indicators.note: bale out signals that the letters of bale are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot bales out after the plane's wing clips a peak, which is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Something palpable can be felt and so is plainly evident.

clue.text: Spur on bosses to become intellectuals

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge or spur them
heads are bosses, chiefs

explanation.surface: Urging managers to become clever thinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal word means bookish, highbrow people.

clue.text: Has cute way, dancing, but shows lack of modesty

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Has cute way, dancing, but shows lack of modesty', gives HASCUTE plus 'way' for the anagram; no reading of 'way' supplies the needed N, so a word is probably misread and no scan is available.
annotationWithheld.clue: Has cute way, dancing, but shows lack of modesty

clue.text: An old offender taken from the street to prison camp

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
an old lag is a long-serving convict

explanation.surface: A habitual criminal is removed from the road and sent to a detention camp.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG alone means an old convict in British slang; the clue's 'old' belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stalag was a German camp for prisoners of war.

clue.text: Condition of dehydration medico should follow

indicators.note: the word for should follows after the doctor's abbreviation

parts.note: DR, doctor, is a medico
ought means should

explanation.surface: A doctor's advice that dehydration should be checked.
explanation.definitionFit: A long lack of rain leaves land parched and dry.

clue.text: He's taken the top from the hill?

parts.note: a cap is a top or lid
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone has removed the summit from a hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's taken' reads as 'he has taken (someone)', which describes one who seizes a prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: The one who holds a prisoner is the person who has taken them.

clue.text: Around a hundred square metres let perhaps, in ring — divided into small areas

parts.note: an are is a metric unit of land area, 100 square metres
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: the shuffled let is placed around the single letter a
perhaps signals that let is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A small plot let out within a circle, carved into little patches.
explanation.walkthrough: LTE, the anagram of LET from 'perhaps', goes 'Around' A to make LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A biological term for a surface marked off into many small spaces or patches.

clue.text: This officer arrives as a result of alarm I'd set off

indicators.note: the letters of alarm I'd are set off, sent into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer turns up because a warning bell was triggered.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior naval rank is a commanding officer of a fleet.

clue.text: A warning — rationality is absent!

parts.note: mind is reason, rationality
out means away, absent

explanation.surface: An alert that someone has lost their reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A cry of 'look out' or 'careful' warns of danger.

clue.text: Smelly, and has nothing on top

indicators.note: nothing sits on the top piece, so it comes first in the across entry

parts.note: O, zero, is nothing
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: Something smelly that wears nothing on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for rank or fetid, giving off a bad odour.

clue.text: Makes enquiries about relative's food

indicators.note: the enquiring word goes about the relative, enclosing it

parts.note: to pump someone is to question them persistently
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Someone asking questions about a family member's cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: These large orange gourds are eaten in pies and soups.

clue.text: Blunders, making these garments

definitions.meaning: baggy knee-length knickers once worn by women

explanation.surface: Mistakes in making clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A howler and an old-fashioned style of baggy underwear share the same plural name.

clue.text: Nag carrying two lads, we hear

indicators.note: we hear it spoken, so the lads' names give a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Harry and Dan are two boys' names

explanation.surface: A horse bearing two boys on its back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nag' suggests a horse; it is the scolding woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding, bad-tempered old woman is a shrew or nag.

clue.text: Hugely unpleasant when he's made to leave

indicators.note: the letters of he are made to leave the word hugely, taken out of it

explanation.surface: Someone is very unhappy that he has been thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: H and E are scattered in HUGELY; removing both leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hideous or nasty, as in an ugly scene.

clue.text: Eleven on a ship damaged by swordfish

indicators.note: eleven comes on, before, the rest in the across entry

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the words a ship are damaged, their letters wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A team of eleven aboard a vessel wrecked by a big fish.
explanation.walkthrough: PHIAS is the anagram of A SHIP from 'damaged'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin genus name for the large billed ocean fish.

clue.text: Thus I secure cover, with many gold coins

indicators.note: so and I secure the cover between them, holding it in place

parts.note: so means thus
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: Someone fastening a lid on a stash of gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman and Byzantine gold pieces, plural of solidus.

clue.text: Hat that's useful in the garden

definitions.meaning: a glass or plastic cover put over young plants

explanation.surface: A hat that a gardener finds handy.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for bell names both a bell-shaped hat and a bell-shaped plant cover.

clue.text: Don't prevaricate when told to go

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I arrived'
someone sent has been told to go

explanation.surface: Advice to stop dithering when ordered away.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an imperative: stop dodging, say yes.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree openly rather than equivocate.

clue.text: Submission apropos conversion, ultimately successful

indicators.note: a conversion of apropos turns its letters into a different arrangement
ultimately points to the final letter of successful

explanation.surface: An offer concerning a religious conversion that finally succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion put forward for consideration is a submission.

clue.text: Fishes for giant squid, initially

parts.note: a troll is a giant of Scandinavian folklore

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of squid

explanation.surface: Angling for a giant squid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishes for giant squid' reads as angling; 'Fishes' is the definition and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail a baited line behind a boat is a way of fishing.

clue.text: Stand late round and duck the issue

indicators.note: stand round together signal turning the letters of late round into a new order
round, with stand, tells you to turn the letters of late about

explanation.surface: Someone stands a late round of drinks and dodges the question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck the issue' reads as evading; 'duck' is the definition and 'the issue' means the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A small freshwater dabbling bird of the wildfowl family.

clue.text: Bud opening at one point in one flowering plant, then another

indicators.note: the bud's start and the point go in the plant word

parts.note: an iris is a flowering plant

indicators.note: the opening of bud is its first letter

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A bud opening at one spot on a plant, then on a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another flowering plant, picking up the earlier phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Candytuft is a garden flower, a second bloom after the first.

clue.text: A problem for girl caught between two men.

indicators.note: the girl and the catch sit between the two men

parts.note: HE is a man, the first of the pair
HE again, the second man
Ada is a girl's name
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A girl trapped between two suitors has a dilemma.
explanation.definitionFit: A source of worry or trouble, a pain.

clue.text: Flyer's skis turning out, then in

indicators.note: then means the second piece follows the first
the letters of skis turn out in a new order

explanation.surface: A skier's skis splay outwards and then turn inwards.
explanation.walkthrough: SISK is the anagram of SKIS from 'turning out'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small yellow-green finch, a bird.

clue.text: By design chap gets noisy

parts.note: a plan is a design
a gent is a chap

explanation.surface: A man deliberately becomes loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By design' reads as 'on purpose'; 'By' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud and resonant, often with a plaintive ring.
